options.text: Does not comply, 1 in 2000 is looser than 1 in 5000

questions.topic: The purpose of a control point
questions.learningObjective: Explain control point stability
questions.stem: Biologist Quinn explains why control points must be stable and undisturbed.

answer.exemplar: Stable, undisturbed control points keep their known coordinates valid over time, so later surveys can rely on them without re-establishing the reference.

questions.explanation: Stability preserves the known coordinates, making the control point useful for future work.

questions.topic: Great-circle distance and the rhumb-line contrast
questions.learningObjective: Identify a rhumb line on a chart
questions.stem: Biologist Sam identifies which line on a Mercator chart is a rhumb line.

options.text: A curved line crossing meridians at varying angles
A line along a meridian only
A line along a parallel only
A straight line crossing meridians at a constant angle

questions.explanation: On Mercator, a rhumb line is straight and crosses all meridians at the same angle.
questions.hint: Rhumb line is straight on Mercator.

questions.topic: Cell count of a digital elevation model
questions.learningObjective: Compute DEM cell count with units
questions.stem: Biologist Tara has a DEM covering 1 km by 0.5 km at 10 m resolution; how many cells?
questions.explanation: One hundred cells along the kilometre side times fifty along the half-kilometre side gives five thousand cells.
questions.hint: Divide each side by resolution, then multiply.
